title: Telemetry-driven Rollback Advisor for Experimental Rollouts
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: Experimental rollouts (canaries, A/B tests, shadow lanes) currently rely on static alerting and manual judgment to abort or roll back. That delays remediation and increases blast radius when subtle regressions (quality drift, distribution shift, latency tail) are only visible in aggregate telemetry.

Motivation: Provide a lightweight, explainable advisor that continuously scores running experiments using multi-signal telemetry windows and recommends safe aborts or automatic quarantines. The advisor is conservative by default (suggest-only) and integrates with the rollout controller to optionally trigger automated actions for high-confidence failures.

What this PR delivers: A new rollback advisor component that: 1) ingests existing rollout telemetry (latency, p75/p95/p99, error rates, inference-quality deltas from eval hooks, and custom experiment metrics), 2) computes a composite risk score with signal-aware weights and a tunable decay window, 3) emits recommendations (suggest_abort, warn, ok) with rationale traces and contributing signals, and 4) exposes a lightweight HTTP webhook API for the rollout controller to poll or subscribe.

Design highlights: - Conservative default policy: suggestions are non-authoritative. Auto-abort requires an explicit rollout annotation. - Explainability: Each recommendation includes the top-3 contributing signals and a short human-readable rationale so SREs and PMs can triage. - Debiasing: The scorer applies cohort-balancing heuristics to avoid false positives when traffic slices are small or skewed. - Safeguards: A quorum-based suppression prevents noisy signals from flipping status during transient blips. - Backfill simulator: an offline replay harness (tests/integration) verifies decision stability over historical traffic.

Developer checklist (in-PR): [x] unit tests for scorer logic; [x] end-to-end integration test with a synthetic canary; [x] docs and example config; [x] presubmit CI; [ ] perf microbench (scheduled).

Usage example (rollout annotation snippet):

  rollout:
    name: my-model-exp
    annotations:
      rollback.advisor/redwood-enabled: "true"
      rollback.advisor/auto-abort: "off"  # options: off|manual-approve|auto-on-critical
      rollback.advisor/threshold: "0.72"

(Annotations control whether the rollout controller will apply suggestions automatically.)

Commit summary: - 7a1d2b3: initial rollback advisor module, public interfaces, and HTTP webhook - 9b4c6d0: telemetry scorer implementation (multi-signal, decay windows) - 0f3e8a1: controller integration: poller and lightweight decision cache - d2c4b77: tests: integration harness with synthetic canary replay - f8a9b21: docs and example rollout annotation; tuning notes; CI fixes

Files changed (high level): - controllers/rollback_advisor.go: new controller that coordinates poll/push and decision caching - telemetry/scorer/scorer.go: multi-signal scoring logic and debiasing heuristics - telemetry/metrics_schema.yaml: schema additions for experiment metrics and quality deltas - docs/rollouts/telemetry-rollback-advisor.md: design + tuning guide + FAQ - examples/experiments/ab-safe-quickstart.yaml: example rollout annotation and sample metrics - tests/integration/rollback_advisor_test.go: replay harness and stable-decision assertions - ci/presubmit-checks.yaml: added integration job entry

Small illustrative snippet (scorer config, for reference):

  scorer:
    window: 120s
    signals:
      - name: p95_latency
        weight: 0.35
      - name: error_rate
        weight: 0.4
      - name: quality_delta
        weight: 0.25
    cohort_balance_threshold: 30
    suppression_quorum: 0.6

Testing notes: - Integration harness replays several historical canaries and asserts that the advisor produces the same recommendation for >= 95% of time windows. - We added guardrail tests that simulate small-cohort skew to validate debiasing heuristics. - One flaky test was stabilized by increasing the metric aggregation window; documented in the commit.

Review conversation (summary): - Ethan Patel: "Concerned about false positives when live traffic is highly skewed. Please add a tuning guide and default cohort_balance_threshold." -> Addressed: added docs and changed default to 30. - Sara Nguyen: "How will this interact with existing alerting? Could we get duplicate noise?" -> Reply: advisor emits a separate recommendation stream; we added a mapping example in docs to dedupe with PagerDuty rules and a short-lived label to indicate advisory vs authoritative. - Diego Morales: "Suggest adding an opt-in path for auto-abort tied to customer SLA tiers." -> Added rollout annotation auto-abort modes and documented fallback behavior. - Sara Nguyen (approval): "Reviewed security around webhook auth and decision payloads; looks good. Approving."

CI summary: - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests: initially failed (race in replay harness), rerun -> pass - linters: pass - e2e-smoke: pass - perf-bench: queued (no blocker) Overall ci_status: pass

Operational considerations: - Default behavior is non-disruptive. Customers must opt-in to automated actions. - Telemetry ingestion depends on the existing metrics pipeline; we added conservative retention and a small memory cap for in-memory windows. - We should run this behind a feature flag for the first month to collect operational telemetry (false-positive rate, decision latency).

Merge: Squash merged on 2026-02-22 via GitHub UI by Maya Chen. Release note included below.

Rationale for uniqueness: This PR focuses on explainable, telemetry-led advisory behavior (suggest-only by default) and a small, auditable webhook integration, rather than an all-or-nothing auto-abort system. It aims to reduce human reaction time to degradations while keeping rollouts safe by default.

release_notes:
Add a telemetry-driven rollback advisor that suggests safe aborts for experimental rollouts. The advisor is suggest-only by default; auto-abort is gated via rollout annotations. Includes docs, example configs, and an offline replay harness.

Operational impact: opt-in; monitor advisor false-positive rate before enabling auto-abort for production rollouts.
